scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After a maintenance window, routes for 19.0.0.0/8, 39.0.0.0/8,
and 90.0.0.0/8 became less stable in r1's RIB. r3 reports
losing an OSPF neighbor. Find the affected link.

injection.action: bring down the link toward r9

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r3 link toward r9
Mechanism: r3 is r9's ONLY backbone neighbor (r9's other
  interface is a stub LAN). r9 owns the 19.0.0.0/8 and
  90.0.0.0/8 prefixes. With the link down, the adjacency
  drops and r9 is fully isolated -- its prefixes disappear
  from the backbone RIBs.
Localization: r3 (eth toward r9)
Root cause: backbone link r3<->r9 is down
Fix: bring the link back up

line.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component**: r3's physical/kernel interface eth0 (segment J, the 39.0.0.0/8 link connecting r3 to r9).

**Mechanism**: r3.eth0 is in kernel state DOWN — the Linux interface flags are `<BROADCAST,MULTICAST>` with no UP or RUNNING flags. Because the link is down, no OSPF Hellos can be sent or received on that segment. Consequently, r3 has no OSPF adjacency with r9, and r9's locally-originated prefixes — 19.1.x.0/24 loopbacks (advertised as 19.0.0.0/8 in the OSPF domain), 39.0.0.0/8 (eth0 connected), and 90.0.0.0/8 (eth1 connected) — never make it into the OSPF LSDB that r3 floods toward r1. All three prefixes are absent from r1's RIB exactly as reported. r9's eth0 is fully operational (UP/RUNNING, 39.1.1.2/8), confirming the fault is strictly on r3's side.

**Localization**: r3, interface eth0 (segment J). FRR itself confirms "eth0 is down / OSPF not enabled on this interface." The kernel link-down timestamp is 2026/08/02 23:09:38 — matching the maintenance window. The interface has recorded zero link-up events since that moment.

**Root cause**: r3's eth0 was left administratively/operationally down after the maintenance window, severing the r3–r9 OSPF adjacency and withdrawing all r9-originated routes from the rest of the topology.

**Corrective fix**: On r3, run `ip link set eth0 up`. The OSPF adjacency between r3 (39.1.1.1) and r9 (39.1.1.2) will re-establish, and prefixes 19.0.0.0/8, 39.0.0.0/8, and 90.0.0.0/8 will be re-advertised into the LSDB and appear in r1's RIB within one OSPF convergence cycle.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names r3's eth0 on the 39.0.0.0/8 segment as the down link to r9, correctly identifying the r3<->r9 affected link.
The report explicitly states that r9's prefixes (19.0.0.0/8, 39.0.0.0/8, 90.0.0.0/8) are absent from r1's RIB and never make it into the LSDB, satisfying recognition of prefix loss.
Proposes bringing r3's eth0 back up (ip link set eth0 up), which directly restores the link and OSPF adjacency as required.

The investigator collected interface state and OSPF neighbor/RIB evidence showing r3.eth0 is kernel-down and r9-originated prefixes are absent from r1; the writeup's conclusions follow logically though one r9-interface output is not fully shown in the log.
